requirements.text: md t-cli cloud enable --owner <email> detects the current project and refuses execution outside a configured project, then delegates provisioning to the MDT-201 management service.

md t-cli cloud enable resolves a trusted service profile, authenticates to the operator audience, and checks service readiness and compatible capabilities before provisioning or writing CONFIG_DIR connection state.
a real 503 service_not_ready response leaves CONFIG_DIR connection state unchanged and exits with an actionable message; 503 is a failure case, not the default Worker state.

successful enablement provisions exactly one cloud project using the project code, initial owner identity, and a next number above existing tickets, then writes the non-secret CONFIG_DIR connection commit-last.
re-running enable for a valid connection reports the existing cloud project UUID and performs no second provisioning mutation.
md t-cli cloud login obtains or refreshes the personal Access session without modifying connection state or membership; login alone does not assign this clone to a project.

md t-cli cloud connect <cloud-project-uuid> consumes an existing UUID, authenticates to the coordination audience, verifies membership, writes CONFIG_DIR connection state commit-last, reports the verified role, and never provisions.
a teammate who clones a bound project authenticates, runs connect with the existing UUID, and uses the cloud project without running enable or provisioning again.

md t-cli cloud status distinguishes absent/local-only, enabled-ready, disabled, malformed, untrusted, authentication-required, forbidden, unavailable, suspended, stale, and incompatible states where supported by the shared contract.

md t-cli cloud doctor reports redacted actionable checks for project context, CONFIG_DIR connection state, trusted origin, credential availability, service readiness, membership, and coordinator reachability.
md t-cli cloud members list shows project members and roles only to an authorized owner.
md t-cli cloud members add <principal> --kind human|machine --role <role> adds or updates normalized membership through the MDT-201 service without accepting a password or token.
md t-cli cloud members remove <principal> --kind human|machine revokes membership and requires confirmation unless --yes is supplied.
machine membership accepts a verified non-secret machine principal id and never accepts or prints its client secret.

md t-cli cloud credentials install <credential-ref> --client-id <id> reads the client secret from a hidden interactive prompt or stdin, never from argv, and writes only to the owner-only CONFIG_DIR credential store.
md t-cli cloud credentials status <credential-ref> and credentials remove <credential-ref> expose only redacted diagnostic views; remove requires confirmation unless --yes is supplied.

md t-cli cloud disable [--yes] delegates to the MDT-201 disable procedure, retains the connection as disabled, keeps ticket creation fail-closed, and never silently resumes local number allocation. There is no permanent-detach command in this ticket.

md t-cli cloud migrate-legacy [--yes] explicitly imports a legacy repository project.cloudSync binding into CONFIG_DIR, rejects conflicts with existing state, leaves repository files unchanged, and requires confirmation unless --yes is supplied.
every cloud command supports human, --json, and --yaml output conventions.
every cloud command maps failures to stable non-zero exit codes through one centralized documented exit-code mapping; process.exit decisions are not scattered across command handlers.
confirmation is required for member removal, credential removal, disable, and legacy migration unless --yes is supplied; non-interactive execution never hangs waiting for input.
md t-cli cloud --help and the generated guide expose all approved subcommands and no provider-specific user workflow.

active cloud connection state, the cloud project UUID, the service origin, and credentials are written only to CONFIG_DIR; .mdt-config.toml and the global project registry never hold active cloud state.
cli code contains no allocation, membership, retry, project-binding, credential-storage, or authorization business logic; every lifecycle operation delegates to the MDT-201 management service.
local-only project commands retain current behavior when the cloud command group is unused or no connection exists.
wrangler remains an operator deployment tool; command help does not instruct teammates to edit uuids manually or use provider-specific user workflows.

no access token, service-token secret, jwt, cookie, authorization header, client secret, or reusable join credential appears in cli output (human/json/yaml), argv, --guide output, logs, repository files, the global registry, or CONFIG_DIR files outside the owner-only credential store.
the client secret is read from a hidden interactive prompt or stdin and is never accepted as an argv value.
one centralized documented cli exit-code mapping owns process.exit decisions for the cloud command group.
a failed readiness, auth, provisioning, or membership step leaves CONFIG_DIR connection state unchanged.
two independent CONFIG_DIR clients connect to the same cloud uuid without a second provisioning.
disabled, malformed, and untrusted connections fail closed; ticket creation does not silently fall back to local numbering.
a 503 service_not_ready response during enable or any protected operation is surfaced as an actionable failure and never written as enabled.
non-interactive execution (no tty) of a command requiring confirmation exits non-zero with an actionable message instead of hanging.
repeated enable on an already-valid connection performs no provisioning mutation and reports the existing uuid.
migrate-legacy rejects a conflict with an existing non-absent CONFIG_DIR connection without writing.
credential install with a malformed or empty secret fails closed without creating a partial credential file.
connect rejects an unknown or revoked uuid with a forbidden/authentication failure and writes no connection state.

scenarios.title: enable refuses outside a project
scenarios.given: given the cwd is not inside a configured mdt project
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud enable --owner owner@example.com is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero with NO_PROJECT_CONTEXT and writes no connection state

scenarios.title: login does not change connection or membership
scenarios.given: given any connection state when absent or enabled
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud login is run
scenarios.then: then the personal access session is obtained or refreshed and CONFIG_DIR connection state and membership are unchanged

scenarios.title: status distinguishes contract states
scenarios.given: given connection states absent/enabled/disabled/malformed/untrusted and coordinator states authentication-required/forbidden/unavailable/suspended/stale/incompatible
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud status is run
scenarios.then: then each state is reported with a distinct actionable message and exit code

scenarios.title: members list requires owner
scenarios.given: given a non-owner coordination credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud members list is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero with forbidden and lists no members

scenarios.title: members add rejects secret input
scenarios.given: given an owner credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud members add machine-principal --kind machine --role member is run
scenarios.then: then upsert carries only the non-secret principal id and the secret is never accepted or printed

scenarios.title: every command supports json and yaml
scenarios.given: given any cloud subcommand
scenarios.when: when run with --json or --yaml
scenarios.then: then it emits valid structured output with no secret values

scenarios.title: members remove requires confirmation
scenarios.given: given a tty and an owner credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud members remove alice@example.com --kind human is run without --yes
scenarios.then: then it prompts for confirmation and only removes after confirmation; with --yes it removes without prompting

scenarios.title: credential remove requires confirmation
scenarios.given: given a tty and an installed credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud credentials remove runtime-a is run without --yes
scenarios.then: then it prompts and only removes after confirmation; with --yes it removes without prompting

scenarios.title: enable checks readiness before provisioning
scenarios.given: given a trusted profile and a worker returning 503 service_not_ready
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud enable --owner owner@example.com is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero with an actionable unavailable message and leaves CONFIG_DIR connection state unchanged

scenarios.title: enable provisions and writes CONFIG_DIR commit-last
scenarios.given: given an operator-audience credential and a ready worker
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud enable --owner owner@example.com is run
scenarios.then: then exactly one provision call is made and CONFIG_DIR connection is written while .mdt-config.toml and the registry are unchanged

scenarios.title: repeated enable performs no second provisioning
scenarios.given: given an existing valid enabled connection
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud enable --owner owner@example.com is run again
scenarios.then: then it reports the existing uuid and performs zero provision calls

scenarios.title: connect writes state only after membership verifies
scenarios.given: given an existing cloud uuid and a coordination credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud connect <uuid> is run
scenarios.then: then it authenticates to the coordination audience, probes membership, writes CONFIG_DIR state commit-last, reports the role, and makes zero provision calls

scenarios.title: writes nothing on revoked or unknown uuid
scenarios.given: given a uuid that the coordinator reports as forbidden or not found
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud connect <uuid> is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero and writes no CONFIG_DIR connection state

scenarios.title: teammate connects without enabling
scenarios.given: given two isolated CONFIG_DIR directories and one enabled project
scenarios.when: when the second client runs mdt-cli cloud connect <uuid>
scenarios.then: then both installations operate against the same cloud uuid and the second performs zero provision calls

scenarios.title: doctor reports redacted actionable checks
scenarios.given: given an enabled connection and an installed credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud doctor is run
scenarios.then: then it reports project context, connection state, trusted origin, credential availability, readiness, membership, and reachability with no secret value present

scenarios.title: credential install reads secret from stdin not argv
scenarios.given: given a non-tty stdin containing the secret
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud credentials install runtime-a --client-id cid is run
scenarios.then: then the secret is read from stdin, written only to the owner-only CONFIG_DIR credential store, never printed, and an empty secret fails closed with no partial file

scenarios.title: credential status is redacted
scenarios.given: given an installed credential
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud credentials status runtime-a is run
scenarios.then: then only the non-secret principal id and kind are shown and the secret is absent from stdout, json, and yaml

scenarios.title: disable retains disabled state
scenarios.given: given an enabled connection
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud disable --yes is run
scenarios.then: then CONFIG_DIR connection state becomes disabled, ticket creation remains fail-closed, and local numbering does not resume

scenarios.title: migrate-legacy rejects conflicts and leaves repo untouched
scenarios.given: given a legacy repository binding and an existing non-absent CONFIG_DIR connection
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud migrate-legacy --yes is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero with a conflict and writes nothing; on success it imports CONFIG_DIR state only and leaves repository files unchanged

scenarios.title: failures map through one exit-code table
scenarios.given: given authentication, authorization, configuration, readiness, network, and coordinator failures
scenarios.when: when any cloud command fails
scenarios.then: then the exit code comes from one centralized documented mapping and no handler calls process.exit inline

scenarios.title: non-interactive confirmation does not hang
scenarios.given: given no tty and a command requiring confirmation without --yes
scenarios.when: when the command is run
scenarios.then: then it exits non-zero with an actionable message instead of waiting for input

scenarios.title: help and guide expose approved commands
scenarios.given: given the installed cli
scenarios.when: when mdt-cli cloud --help or the generated guide is rendered
scenarios.then: then it lists enable, login, connect, status, doctor, members, credentials, disable, migrate-legacy and no provider-specific user workflow

obligations.title: cloud command group delegates every lifecycle op to MDT-201 service
active cloud state lives only in CONFIG_DIR; .mdt-config.toml and registry untouched
one centralized exit-code mapping; no inline process.exit in cloud handlers
disable retains disabled and fail-closed; migrate-legacy conflict-safe
help and generated guide expose the approved command set only
client secret never in argv, output, logs, or non-credential-store files
connect verifies membership and never provisions; enable idempotent
coordination guide documents owner enable and teammate connect journeys

createManagementService wires the service against a fake coordinator

Migrate-legacy against an existing connection writes nothing

repeated enable reports existing uuid with zero provision calls
login obtains a session without changing connection state
connect verifies membership and writes state with zero provisions
two isolated CONFIG_DIR clients share one uuid via connect
status distinguishes every contract-supported state
doctor reports redacted actionable checks
members list/add/remove with owner authorization and no secret
credentials install/status/remove with secret from stdin only

every command honors --json and --yaml with no secret

local-only ticket commands behave identically when no cloud connection exists or cloud group is unused
